Graduate programs are administered by the Case Western Reserve University School of Graduate Studies.
PhD in Civil Engineering
With a PhD in Civil Engineering from Case School of Engineering, you’ll be prepared to develop innovations for a cleaner environment, more reliable infrastructure, and a safer, more sustainable world.
Alignment
None
Degree: Doctor of Philosophy
Major: Civil Engineering
In our program, you’ll hone your engineering skills while learning how to lead projects involving transportation systems, schools and office buildings, bridges, dams and industrial plants.
You’ll have ample opportunities for cross-disciplinary collaborations and research with faculty who are experts in engineering mechanics, environmental engineering, infrastructure performance and reliability, geotechnical engineering and structural engineering.
Our program will prepare you for highly specialized careers in civil and environmental engineering—from academia to industrial, governmental, construction and private-consulting organizations. Where will your PhD take you?

Degree FAQs
How do I apply?
Engineering graduate degrees are administered by the university's School of Graduate Studies. Visit the school’s website to apply and learn more about admissions requirements, deadlines and more.
The GRE is being waived for 2021-2022 applicants due to the COVID-19 pandemic.
What are my degree requirements?
Review the university's General Bulletin for specific course requirements.
How long will it take me to complete my PhD?
Typically, students take four to five years to complete their degree. If you come into the program directly from an undergraduate program, you can expect to invest about five years working on your PhD. If you enter the program with a master’s degree, you can complete your PhD in four years.
